articles.headline: Rubio defends Iran war as necessary protection against nuclear threats
articles.title: Rubio says Trump's war against Iran not 'necessarily popular' but needed to stop a nuclear threat
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the military campaign against Iran on November 7, 2026, stating it was launched to neutralize nuclear dangers despite political fallout. The conflict has impacted the economy and contributed to Republican losses in Congress. Meanwhile, mediators are attempting to revive diplomatic talks as regional tensions remain high and military strikes continue.
articles.description: America's top diplomat offered a robust defence of the more than eight-month-old war even as voters blamed Mr. Trump's policies for the hit to their pocketbooks, including higher energy prices that stemmed from disruptions to shipments in the Strait of Hormuz

articles.headline: Trump announces possible trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin next week

articles.summary: Foreign ministers from the Group of Seven industrialised nations gathered in Paris on November 9, 2026, for two days of talks. European powers aimed to press U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio for a fair settlement in Russia's war on Ukraine and to deter further military action against Iran. articles.headline: COP31 climate summit opens in Antalya amid geopolitical tensions
articles.title: COP31 opens as climate and geopolitical pressures mount
articles.summary: United Nations climate talks began on November 9, 2026, in Antalya, Turkiye, with over 100,000 attendees expected. articles.headline: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over relationship with Alice Huang

The inquiry follows reports that the woman sought to obtain technology secrets, sparking bipartisan concern in the United States Congress regarding advanced artificial intelligence exports.
articles.description: Huang has confirmed he had been having an affair with a woman accused of spying for China.

articles.headline: Aramco Tower hit in Saudi capital as Houthi strikes intensify
articles.title: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
articles.summary: The Aramco Tower in Riyadh suffered minor damage following an air attack confirmed by Houthi media on Saturday. The Saudi energy ministry reported no casualties, though BBC Verify footage showed extensive destruction. The strike occurred amid renewed conflict following the collapse of an informal ceasefire in July, leading to over 1,600 deaths according to United Nations figures.
articles.description: Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows damage to the building in the capital's central financial district.

articles.headline: Iran warns US of severe military escalation amid stalled bilateral negotiations
articles.title: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that Tehran will launch heavy attacks against American forces if the United States resumes hostilities, issuing an ultimatum during an ongoing eight-month conflict. articles.description: President Trump warns that US forces are 'locked and loaded' and ready to strike, if necessary.

articles.headline: ANC records historic low in South Africa local elections
articles.title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election
articles.summary: South Africa's governing African National Congress won only 31 percent of the vote in local elections, marking a sharp decline from previous years. Party secretary-general Fikile Mbalula described the outcome as catastrophic, citing high living costs and infrastructure issues. The Democratic Alliance came second with 25 percent, while former president Jacob Zuma's MK party placed third with 10 percent.
articles.description: President Cyril Ramaphosa says the verdict must be respected, while the party's secretary-general calls the outcome "catastrophic".

articles.headline: Donald Trump vows political comeback after Republicans lose control of Congress
articles.title: Trump vows comeback as bitter showdown with Congress looms
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump vowed a political comeback on November 8, 2026, after his Republican Party lost control of both houses of Congress in midterm elections. The outcome leaves Mr. Trump hamstrung for his remaining two-year term and facing investigations. articles.summary: Multiple witnesses confirmed that Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District was struck and an Aramco tower sustained facade and glass damage on November 8, 2026. Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki stated that air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by Houthi forces toward the Saudi capital. articles.summary: Russian investigative outlet Novaya Gazeta ended operations due to state pressure, holding its final editorial meeting on Monday. Labeled a foreign agent last September, the publication struggled after banks halted reader donations. Cofounder Dmitry Muratov criticized the closure in Moscow, while the Kremlin described it as a normal change. United Nations human rights chief Volker Turk called the shutdown a devastating blow to independent media.
articles.description: The paper was one of the few remaining outlets in Russia that criticised Moscow's war on Ukraine.

articles.headline: Republican congressman Thomas Massie forces impeachment vote on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.title: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth
articles.summary: Republican Representative Thomas Massie plans to force a House vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, alleging constitutional violations regarding hostilities in Iran. articles.headline: French government moves planned minimum wage increase forward to quell protests
articles.title: France accelerates minimum wage hike in bid to quell protest
articles.summary: The French government announced it will move a planned 1.6 percent minimum wage increase forward by a month to December 1, 2026, aiming to quell ongoing protests over the cost of living. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu detailed the hike during a press conference on Monday. The adjustment raises the monthly minimum wage by 24 euros to 1,502 euros, though major labor unions dismissed the measure as insufficient.
articles.description: Unions slam the increase as insufficient, as the government seeks to defuse the unrest ahead of upcoming elections.

articles.title: Israeli President picks Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu rival, to try to form government
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government following an inconclusive election. Eisenkot, a 66-year-old former military chief, must navigate complex coalition negotiations within a 28-day window after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in the October 27 vote while remaining the largest bloc in parliament.

articles.headline: Ousted leader Sheikh Hasina requests new passport to return from exile

articles.headline: Houthi authorities report forty-four deaths from airstrikes near Sanaa
articles.title: Houthi rebels say at least 44 killed in airstrike near Yemeni capital

articles.title: More than 50,000 displaced by deadly Ethiopia border clashes

articles.title: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant relying on generators again after losing external power supply
articles.summary: The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in southeastern Ukraine lost its external electricity supply after the Ferosplavna line disconnected, according to the International Atomic Energy Agency and plant management. Facility operators activated emergency diesel generators to maintain reactor cooling systems. articles.headline: Poland begins national mourning following fatal mass shooting in Krakow
articles.title: Poland mourns six killed in attack as authorities launch ‘terrorism’ probe
articles.summary: Poland initiated two days of national mourning after a twenty-four-year-old armed suspect killed six people in central Krakow. The national prosecutor's office opened a terrorism investigation into the shooting, while three additional bodies were found at the suspect's residence. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski stated that the attacker was influenced by far-right ideologies following the tragic events.
articles.description: 'Terrorism' investigation launched after government officials say suspect likely influenced by far-right ideology.

articles.headline: Democratic candidates flip five state attorney general offices in midterm elections
articles.title: Democratic wins in State AG races give Trump a new headache

articles.headline: Russian overnight strikes leave hundreds of thousands without electricity in Ukraine

articles.summary: Two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after striking naval mines while navigating unauthorised routes, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. articles.headline: OpenAI secures funding valuation of $1.25 trillion
articles.title: OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO
articles.summary: According to Bloomberg, OpenAI has reached a valuation of $1.25 trillion after securing another $11 billion in funding. articles.headline: Heavy rains and flooding destroy tens of thousands of displaced tents in Gaza
articles.title: Floods in Gaza leave tens of thousands without shelter
articles.summary: Severe storms and heavy rains damaged shelters and flooded seventy thousand tents across the Gaza Strip, affecting tens of thousands of displaced Palestinians in November 2026. articles.description: What do the results tell us about American voters’ attitudes towards President Donald Trump? What do they mean for Democrats and Republicans? What lies ahead for Democrats? Why are these results so important for the rest of the world?

articles.description: On his social media site, Donald Trump praised Susie Wiles and said she’d continue working for his political organisation

articles.headline: New Zealand election ends in deadlock with no clear winner
articles.title: New Zealanders won’t know for weeks who won election as neither side secures clear victory
articles.summary: New Zealand faces weeks of uncertainty following the November 7, 2026, election, which failed to give either major bloc a clear majority. Minor parties, including the newcomer Opportunity party led by Qiulae Wong, hold potential leverage. articles.headline: Atiqa Mir finishes sixth on FIA Karting World Championship debut
articles.title: Atiqa Mir produces overtaking masterclass to finish 6th on FIA World Championship debut

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces capture positions in Lahj and al-Jawf

articles.summary: Yemeni government forces captured Houthi-held positions in Lahj and al-Jawf as part of Operation Dawn of Yemen. articles.description: Yemeni forces claim fresh advances across key fronts as cross-border Houthi attacks surge amid heavy clashes.

articles.headline: Anuj Shrivatri becomes India's 100th chess grandmaster
articles.title: Anuj lights up Indian chess, becomes the 100th GM

articles.headline: Meta expands automated age-estimation technology for teens globally
articles.title: Meta rolls out automated age checks for teens globally

articles.description: AI-powered scans will be used for Instagram accounts starting this month and later extended to Facebook and Threads.

articles.description: Kishore Biyani’s Future Group witnessed meteoric rise before mounting financial troubles pushed it into insolvency

articles.headline: Gunman kills five people during shooting attack in Krakow
articles.title: Gunman kills 5, injures 12 in Poland’s Krakow shooting attack

articles.headline: Nine foreigners arrested in South Africa for allegedly attempting to join Ukraine war

articles.headline: Twenty five killed in Saudi airstrikes in Yemen
articles.title: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike
articles.summary: Media outlets linked to the Houthi movement reported that at least twenty five individuals, including women and children, died following Saudi airstrikes in al-Shariyah. The attack occurred amid resumed major fighting across Yemen between the Houthis and forces supporting the internationally recognised government. The United Nations stated that more than one thousand six hundred people have died since hostilities reignited.
articles.description: Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen, has not commented.

articles.headline: Trump discusses AI safety and Department of Justice actions in interview
articles.title: Trump’s 60 Minutes interview touched on AI safety, threat to arrest an AI exec
articles.summary: During a 60 Minutes interview, former United States President Donald Trump asserted that artificial intelligence risks are manageable and claimed the Department of Justice threatened a major AI executive with imprisonment. Trump declined to name the executive or company involved, while also discussing international competition with China and potential cooperation with Democrats on safety guardrails.
articles.description: Asked about AI executives' warnings about their models' safety on 60 Minutes, Trump said, "I think that the risk is not nearly as real as it- as they talk, and I think the risk can be managed, and it's managed." He claimed the DOJ is managing that risk, saying, "We had a situation where somebody […]

articles.headline: Greek coast guard recovers bodies of dead migrants off Crete
articles.title: Twenty-one migrants die trying to reach Greece’s Crete: authorities
articles.summary: The Greek coast guard recovered twelve dead migrants from a boat south of Crete on November 9, 2026, alongside eight other bodies found in a separate vessel. Maritime authorities rescued roughly forty survivors during emergency operations launched amid strong winds. Crete has increasingly become a primary entry point into the European Union for migrants departing from Libya.
articles.description: Eight bodies were found on one boat and 12 on another, while some 40 people were rescued off both, says Greek Coast Guard

articles.headline: Nvidia board launches probe into Jensen Huang over affair with suspected spy
articles.title: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
articles.summary: Nvidia board of directors has initiated an investigation into Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang following reports he had a romantic relationship with a woman believed by United States intelligence to be a Chinese spy. The 63-year-old billionaire co-founded the artificial intelligence chip giant in 1993, which has grown into one of the world's most valuable companies. The board maintains confidence in his leadership.
articles.description: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.

articles.headline: Disney and Adobe partner to develop custom generative AI models
articles.title: Disney and Adobe are building generative AI tools together
articles.summary: The Walt Disney Company has partnered with Adobe to create proprietary generative artificial intelligence tools tailored for theme parks, cruise lines, and ESPN content. Announced at the Adobe MAX conference, the multiyear agreement gives Disney early access to the Adobe Firefly Foundry platform. According to Adobe, the collaboration aims to build human-centered models trained on character attributes to accelerate production workflows and enhance fan engagement.
articles.description: The Walt Disney Company has teamed up with Adobe to develop proprietary "artist-led" generative AI models to support Disney's production pipeline. The multiyear partnership was announced today at Adobe's MAX conference, and it will see Adobe providing Disney with early access to its latest technologies for everything from Disney's theme parks and cruise line to […]

articles.headline: Senegal human rights group demands inquiry after migrant boat sinking
articles.title: Senegal human rights group demands government action after deadly sinking
articles.summary: A human rights organization in Senegal urged the government to launch a parliamentary inquiry after a migrant boat sank off the coast, resulting in at least 39 deaths. Action for Human Rights and Friendship criticized ongoing migrant shipwrecks despite previous funding announcements. The vessel had departed from Saint-Louis toward Spain before overturning near the Lompoul dunes, with emergency services continuing search operations for missing passengers.
articles.description: Thousands ⁠of people have ⁠died in recent years attempting to reach Spain’s Canary Islands from West Africa.

articles.headline: Los Angeles elects democratic socialist Nithya Raman as mayor
articles.title: Los Angeles mayoral race points to growing sway of democratic socialists
articles.summary: Los Angeles City Council member Nithya Raman defeated incumbent Karen Bass to win the mayoral race, capturing nearly 53 percent of the vote. Raman, who identifies as a democratic socialist, will take office in December. Her victory highlights the growing political influence of democratic socialists across the United States, as candidates increasingly focus on affordability, cost-of-living issues, and municipal governance to attract working-class voters.
articles.description: Nithya Raman taps into frustration with economic and political status quo to become mayor of the second-largest US city.

articles.headline: India reaches milestone of one hundred chess grandmasters
articles.title: Hundredth GM milestone underlines India’s remarkable growth in chess
articles.summary: Anuj Shrivatri became India's one hundredth chess grandmaster by winning the ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship in Ozamiz City, the Philippines. Four decades after Viswanathan Anand secured the country's first title in 1987, India has joined an exclusive group alongside Russia, the United States, and Germany as nations with triple-digit grandmasters.
articles.description: Shrivatri became No. 100 on the Diwali Day. He got his GM title, directly, by winning the ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship at Ozamiz City, the Philippines

articles.headline: Cardiologists seek review of medical device re-use ban to reduce costs
articles.title: Cardiologists seek review of DGHS order banning re-use of single-use medical devices to reduce angioplasty costs
articles.summary: Cardiologists at the Cardiological Society of India Kerala chapter annual conference on Sunday urged a review of a Director General of Health Services order banning the re-use of single-use medical devices. Association leaders warned that prohibiting sterilisation and re-use of equipment like catheters and guidewires will make critical procedures such as angioplasty unaffordable for ordinary patients, while stressing that patient safety and scientific validation must remain paramount.
articles.description: With an increasing proportion of the population requiring advanced cardiac interventions, making complex procedures affordable to ordinary patients has become a major challenge. Permitting the regulated re-use of select interventional devices, wherever scientifically proven safe, could help reduce treatment costs and extend the benefits of modern cardiac care to a wider section of the population, says Cardiological Society of India, Kerala chapter

articles.headline: Nvidia investigates executive links following allegations involving suspected Chinese spy
articles.title: Who is the suspected Chinese spy at centre of the Nvidia investigation?
articles.summary: United States chip manufacturer Nvidia announced an internal investigation following reports that Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang maintained ties with Alice Huang, the former managing director of Singapore-based Megaspeed. According to The New York Times, American officials suspect Alice Huang of intelligence gathering for China. While Chinese authorities dismissed the accusations as groundless, Nvidia stated it is examining all available information to ensure national security remains uncompromised.
articles.description: Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman, had a close relationship with Nvidia boss Jensen Huang, reports say.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will open India's first tilted dome planetarium in Mysuru.
articles.title: PM to open LED dome planetarium in Mysuru on November 13
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate an LED dome planetarium in Mysuru on November 13, 2026. Built at a cost of 118 crore rupees with contributions from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics and the University of Mysore, the facility features approximately 150 to 160 seats. According to local Member of Parliament Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, the project aims to benefit both students and regional tourists.

articles.headline: Karnataka minister Rizwan Arshad defends test reports alleging excessive ethanol blending in petrol.
articles.title: Ethanol blend row: Minister stands firm on claim, demands independent fuel testing
articles.summary: Karnataka Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister Rizwan Arshad defended test reports on November 9, 2026, alleging that petrol samples from major oil marketing companies exceeded the 20% ethanol blending limit. Speaking in Bengaluru, Mr. Arshad criticized oil companies for failing to provide required testing metrics and demanded independent fuel testing. He asserted that state laboratories followed prescribed NABL procedures to protect consumers from potential vehicle damage.
articles.description: It was the OMC laboratories’ failure to provide the required result that raised suspicion; the samples were then sent to NABL-accredited and ISO-certified laboratories, says Rizwan Arshad

articles.headline: Telangana chief minister sets goal to create one crore women millionaires by 2034
articles.title: Revanth sets target of making one crore women millionaires by 2034
articles.summary: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced a government initiative to expand self-help group membership to one crore and elevate members to millionaire status during an event at the Lagacharla Industrial Hub on November 8, 2026. Addressing attendees, he highlighted economic measures including bank-linkage loans totaling ₹79,000 crore, welfare pensions, and expanded business opportunities in sectors like retail and solar power to foster female entrepreneurship.
articles.description: Promises greater economic opportunities for SHG members; says women’s empowerment is central to his government’s policies

articles.headline: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani denies troop deployment to Yemen.
articles.title: Syrian FM says country has no troops in Yemen, won't send any
articles.summary: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani stated on November 9, 2026, that his country has no military forces deployed in Yemen and has no plans to send any. Speaking during a press conference in Amman with Jordanian counterpart Ayman Safadi, Mr. Shaibani dismissed reports from Agence France-Presse regarding secret troop movements. He emphasized that recent defense cooperation agreements with Saudi Arabia are intended strictly for institutional and academic rebuilding.
articles.description: He said the accord with Riyadh, a key backer of Damascus as it seeks to rebuild after more than a decade of civil war, was vital for Syria to rebuild its institutions, including the military

articles.headline: US military launches new task force to disrupt Iranian land supply routes
articles.title: US launches task force to disrupt Iran’s land-based supply routes
articles.summary: The United States military’s Central Command established Task Force Iron Gate to prevent Iran from utilizing ground routes and the Caspian Sea to transport advanced weapons and materials. Based in Tampa, Florida, the new unit expands previous naval blockades. Meanwhile, officials reported explosions near the Strait of Hormuz and damaged oil tankers.
articles.description: The operation is to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport weapons and other materials, US says.

articles.headline: Former antitrust head Jonathan Kanter launches artificial intelligence legal startup FluxCap.
articles.title: Jonathan Kanter is using AI to take on Big Tech
articles.summary: Former Department of Justice Antitrust Division head Jonathan Kanter launched a new tech startup named FluxCap alongside Doha Mekki to provide artificial intelligence tools for antitrust litigation. The platform utilizes large language models to help legal teams sift through discovery materials and build complex cases against major technology companies. According to Mr. Kanter, the technology serves as a vital force multiplier for resource-constrained public and private enforcers challenging powerful corporations.
articles.description: When Jonathan Kanter stepped down as head of the Justice Department's Antitrust Division in 2024, he set out to keep fighting to dismantle illegal monopolies. But this time, he's continuing the fight in the private sector, and with a perhaps unexpected tool: AI. Alongside former acting Antitrust Division chief Doha Mekki, Kanter recently launched a […]

articles.headline: Indian banking stocks surge 1.5% as broader markets pause following six-day rally.
articles.title: Banking stocks rally 1.5% as PSU lenders lead; broader markets pause after six-day bull run
articles.summary: Indian benchmark indices closed marginally higher on November 9, 2026, as investors engaged in profit-booking following a six-session bull run. The Nifty 50 finished up 0.23% at 25,044.65 points while the Sensex gained 0.13% to reach 81,106.58. Banking shares outperformed the broader market trend, led by a 3.73% surge in the Nifty PSU Bank index, while the Indian rupee snapped its six-day winning streak to close flat at 93.90 against the United States dollar.
articles.description: “Indian equities are likely to consolidate in the near term as investors book profits after the sharp rally of over 10% in seven sessions,” says Siddhartha Khemka, head of research, wealth management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services.

articles.headline: ANC records worst-ever result in South African local elections
articles.title: What ‘catastrophic’ South Africa local election results mean for ANC
articles.summary: South Africa’s ruling African National Congress secured 31 percent of the vote in municipal elections, finishing behind the Democratic Alliance in major urban centres such as Johannesburg and Pretoria. Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula called the outcome catastrophic. Political parties face a 14-day negotiation window to form local coalitions amid voter anger over corruption and failing public services.
articles.description: The country is transitioning away from the era of ANC electoral dominance towards a more fragmented political system.

articles.headline: Ramla Ali defeats Mikiah Kreps for first world title
articles.title: British-Somali ‌‌‌‌boxer Ramla Ali defeats Mikiah Kreps for first ⁠⁠⁠⁠world title
articles.summary: British-Somali boxer Ramla Ali claimed the vacant International Boxing Organization and World Boxing Foundation junior featherweight titles after a split-decision victory over American fighter Mikiah Kreps in Arlington, Texas. Although official statistics showed Kreps outlanded her opponent in total blows, two judges scored the bout in favour of Ali, who dedicated the win to her late father.
articles.description: Ali wins a controversial split-decision fight against American Kreps to claim IBO and WBF junior featherweight belts.

articles.headline: Thirteen migrants die after boat sinks off Crete
articles.title: Thirteen migrants die after boat sinks off Crete
articles.summary: At least 13 Sudanese nationals died and 18 others were rescued after a migrant vessel sank roughly 15 nautical miles off the coast of the Greek island of Crete. The Greek coastguard reported that strong winds and a prolonged journey contributed to the disaster. Crete has experienced a significant surge in maritime arrivals this year, surpassing totals from 2025.
articles.description: The Greek coastguard says it has rescued 18 people, all of whom were Sudanese nationals.

articles.headline: Paraguayan police raid home of ousted president Santiago Pena
articles.title: Paraguay raids ex-president’s home: Why a bank crash brought down Pena
articles.summary: Paraguayan authorities searched the mansion of recently removed President Santiago Pena following the collapse of Ueno Bank, which froze savings accounts for nearly three million customers. Pena was detained after the Senate voted to remove him from office. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in to finish the remainder of the presidential term until August 2028.
articles.description: Santiago Pena faces charges of financial crimes following Ueno Bank's collapse, impacting half of Paraguay's population.

articles.headline: Former Paraguay President Santiago Peña charged over bank collapse
articles.title: Paraguay's ousted President charged with crimes linked to collapse of major bank
articles.summary: Prosecutors in Asuncion charged deposed leader Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain following the collapse of Ueno Bank. Judge Humberto Otazu ordered Mr Peña to be held at a military base during investigations. The bank failure froze millions of accounts, triggering Congress to remove Mr Peña and replace him with Pedro Alliana, while public protests and an upcoming teachers union strike persist.
articles.description: In a farewell message released shortly before he was ousted on Friday (November 6), Mr. Peña expressed hope his departure would spare Paraguay further harm

articles.headline: Gaza tent collapse kills four people during heavy rainstorms
articles.title: Four killed in Gaza as sand embankment collapses on tents
articles.summary: Torrential rain on November 8, 2026, caused a sand embankment to collapse onto a displacement camp in central Gaza, killing a woman and three children while injuring six others, according to medics. The incident affected Deir al-Balah, where local authorities reported at least seventy thousand flooded tents. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs received appeals from over twenty-six thousand households regarding shelter damage during the weekend storms.
articles.description: Medics ​said heavy rain late on November 8 washed away a rocky sand ⁠bank abutting a camp for displaced families south of Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza

articles.headline: Syrian foreign ministry confirms troop deployment to Saudi Arabia
articles.title: Syria confirms sending troops to Saudi Arabia amid battle against Houthis
articles.summary: Syria confirmed sending military advisers and special forces to Saudi Arabia for training and consultations following a recent visit by President Ahmed al-Sharaa to Riyadh. The deployment aims to support Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks from Yemen, according to Syrian officials. The cooperation could potentially lead to Syria joining the Mecca Defence Alliance, as Riyadh previously pledged four hundred three million dollars in loans to help rebuild infrastructure damaged by thirteen years of civil war.
articles.description: Syrian officials deny reports Damascus is sending troops to Yemen, but Syrian security integration appears under way

articles.headline: Republican lawmakers prepare for leadership elections in United States Congress
articles.title: Which Republicans are running for minority leadership roles in US Congress?
articles.summary: United States congressional Republicans are holding internal party elections on Tuesday to select minority leaders following midterm losses that handed Democrats control of both legislative chambers starting in January. Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan are competing for House minority leader, while John Thune seeks to lead Senate Republicans. Mike Johnson will step down as House speaker and declined to run for minority leader, though he remains in Congress.
articles.description: Republicans in US House and Senate will hold elections on Tuesday to select leadership after losing their majorities.

articles.headline: Explosion at iron and steel factory near Izmir kills six people
articles.title: Six dead in blast at steel factory near Turkiye’s Izmir: officials
articles.summary: An explosion at the Habas Demir Celik factory near the Turkish city of Izmir resulted in six fatalities and approximately a dozen injuries. The blast occurred during the midday hours and triggered a fire at the industrial plant. Local officials reported that emergency rescue teams were deployed to clear wreckage from the site.
articles.description: Izmir Mayor Cemil Tugay said rescue teams were "continuing their work to remove the collapsed platform" and that those affected were factory workers.

articles.headline: China rejects ‘baseless’ claims it spied on Nvidia boss
articles.title: China rejects ‘baseless’ claims it spied on Nvidia boss
articles.description: China denies spying on Nvidia boss Jensen Huang as the company probes his affair with an alleged intelligence agent.

articles.headline: Telangana health minister directs officials to assess secondary healthcare facility gaps
articles.title: Gaps in services at Telangana’s secondary healthcare facilities to be assessed
articles.summary: Telangana Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha has ordered a comprehensive evaluation of secondary healthcare facilities to improve district-level medical and diagnostic services. During a review meeting in Hyderabad, officials examined proposals from the Administrative Staff College of India to align Community Health Centres and District Hospitals with Indian Public Health Standards.
articles.description: Health Minister Damodar Raja Narasimha directs officials to assess specialist services currently available, departments requiring additional doctors and nursing or paramedical staff, and gaps in diagnostic facilities

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu government announces compensation for families of police personnel killed on duty
articles.title: Tamil Nadu government issues order for ₹1 crore aid to bereaved families of police personnel who die on duty
articles.summary: The government of Tamil Nadu has approved a special compensation of one crore rupees for families of police personnel who die under heroic circumstances during law and order duties. The measure implements an earlier announcement made by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in the Legislative Assembly to boost morale within the Police Department.
articles.description: The decision follows an earlier announcement by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in the Legislative Assembly while moving the demand for grants for the Police Department on the floor of Assembly for the year 2026-2027.

articles.headline: Firecracker smoke triggers respiratory health issues during Deepavali pollution spike
articles.title: Deepavali pollution spike: How does it affect lung function and respiratory health? | Explained
articles.summary: Short-term exposure to firecracker smoke can induce coughing and breathlessness in individuals with asthma or other respiratory conditions, while high pollutant concentrations irritate airways across the general population. India utilizes the Air Quality Index, calculated by the Central Pollution Control Board from eight pollutants including PM2.5 and carbon monoxide, to measure pollution levels and associated health effects.
articles.description: Firecracker smoke releases fine particles and harmful gases that irritate the airways and affect lung health. Experts explain the short- and long-term effects of exposure and whether the damage persists after air quality improves

articles.headline: Rape and murder accused Dilip Roy killed by police in Raiganj encounter
articles.title: Another ‘encounter’ in West Bengal: Rape-murder accused killed in Raiganj
articles.summary: Dilip Roy, a prime suspect in the rape and murder of a thirteen-year-old minor, was shot dead by police during an exchange of gunfire while attempting to flee toward Bihar on November 9, 2026. According to police officials, the incident occurred at around 3:30 a.m. in the Gauri village area after officers located him following the discovery of the victim's mutilated body on November 5.
articles.description: Suvendu Adhikari defended the killing of the accused, saying personnel can fire in self-defence, as he asserted that his government had given the force a free hand to deal with rapists, drug traffickers and infiltrators

articles.headline: Republican coalition shatters following historic midterm election defeats
articles.title: The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now?
articles.summary: Republicans are experiencing severe infighting after suffering massive losses in the 2026 midterms, losing control of both congressional chambers and key state legislatures. Party strategists and leaders like Vice-President JD Vance are divided on whether to maintain Make America Great Again populist policies or moderate. President Donald Trump responded by appointing Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff.
articles.description: Republicans can stick with Trumpism or chart a new path, writes BBC Washington correspondent Daniel Bush.

articles.headline: Chennai hospitals report dozens of cracker-related eye injuries during Deepavali
articles.title: Chennai sees dozens of cracker-related eye injuries; doctors call for caution
articles.summary: Ophthalmologists in Chennai urged caution after receiving dozens of cracker-related eye injuries during Deepavali celebrations on November 8, 2026. The Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital treated around 50 cases, while Sankara Nethralaya and Dr. Agarwals Eye Hospital reported 45 and 20 patients respectively. Doctors stressed the importance of wearing protective eyewear and seeking immediate medical attention for injuries.
articles.description: The Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital received around 50 cases, with about 10 cases having to be admitted, a senior official said.

articles.headline: Polish PM calls deadly Krakow shooting an act of ‘terrorism’
articles.title: Polish PM calls deadly Krakow shooting an act of ‘terrorism’
articles.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk describes a deadly shooting in Krakow that killed six people as an act of ‘terrorism’.

articles.headline: Chennai air quality drops to poor category after Deepavali celebrations
articles.title: Chennai’s air quality deteriorates to ‘poor’ the morning after Deepavali
articles.summary: Chennai experienced a sharp deterioration in air quality, with the Air Quality Index slipping to 213 on the morning of November 9, 2026, according to the Central Pollution Control Board. The decline followed intense firecracker bursting on Deepavali night. Station-wise data showed Manali Village recorded the highest index at 296, while private monitors indicated significantly higher pollution levels during peak celebration hours.
articles.description: Manali Village recorded the highest AQI at 296, followed by Arumbakkam at 265, Kodungaiyur at 215, Royapuram at 184 and Velachery Residential Area at 142

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi challenges Prime Minister Narendra Modi to debate on anti-national claims
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi dares PM to debate him on who is ‘anti-national’
articles.summary: Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to a public debate on November 9, 2026, regarding accusations of anti-national activity. The challenge followed remarks made by Modi to Central Reserve Police Force personnel in Bastar on November 8, 2026, where he warned about intellectual Naxals. The Congress party strongly condemned the Prime Minister's statements, while Bharatiya Janata Party leaders dismissed the challenge.
articles.description: Accusing the PM of branding his political opponents as ‘Naxals’ following his Deepavali speech to CRPF personnel, the Congress leader reiterates his challenge to debate him on ‘who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces’

articles.headline: India witnesses significant reduction in villages lacking 4G connectivity over four years
articles.title: Number of villages without 4G connectivity falls by three-fourths in four years
articles.summary: The number of Indian villages without 4G connectivity dropped significantly from 45,180 in 2022 to 11,372, according to Department of Telecommunications data obtained under the Right to Information Act, 2005. This reduction surpassed the initial target of the Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited 4G saturation project due to complementary private efforts. The improvement highlights the growing importance of mobile broadband amid stagnant wired subscriptions.
articles.description: Data obtained by The Hindu under the Right to Information Act shows a sharp decline in the number of villages without serviceable internet speeds

articles.headline: Pakistani TV anchor Rabia Ahsan shot dead at home in Rawalpindi
articles.title: Pakistani TV anchorperson shot dead at home in Rawalpindi; husband held
articles.summary: Rabia Ahsan, a Pakistani TV anchor and programme host, was shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi on November 8, 2026, according to local media reports. Rawalpindi police took her husband into custody and seized the suspected weapon following the incident in the Gulshanabad area. First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari expressed deep sadness and called for a transparent investigation into the killing.
articles.description: According to the CPO, a male domestic worker at the house told police that the victim's husband had claimed that the gunshot was fired accidentally.

articles.headline: Mumbai records 137 firecracker blazes on Deepavali, injuring two women
articles.title: Mumbai records 137 firecracker-induced blazes on Deepavali, highest single-day tally in years
articles.summary: Mumbai recorded an unprecedented 137 firecracker-induced blazes across the city and suburbs on November 8, 2026, injuring two women, according to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation. The single-day tally exceeded prior yearly festival totals. The surge prompted the Mumbai Fire Brigade to issue urgent safety guidelines and emergency contact numbers, urging residents to burst crackers only in designated open areas and properly supervise children.
articles.description: The sharp rise in incidents prompted the Mumbai Fire Brigade to issue urgent safety guidelines, asking citizens to burst crackers only in open areas away from residential buildings, shops, vehicles, petrol pumps, transformers, and overhead wires.

articles.headline: Explosions reported in southern Iran as two oil tankers catch fire
articles.title: Explosions heard in areas in southern Iran, Iranian media report
articles.summary: Explosions were reported on November 7, 2026, in southern Iran including Qeshm Island, according to Iranian state television, while the Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Officials did not confirm missile strikes, though U.S. forces recently struck the island, raising regional tensions amid ongoing shipping conflicts.
articles.description: State TV said Iranian ‌officials have not confirmed any missile strikes on the areas, while the semi-official Tasnim news agency cited ‌a source as saying that the explosions heard ‌on ⁠Qeshm Island were not related to missile strikes
